docs.title: From a Wi-Fi location to the evidence behind it
docs.text:
A Wi-Fi fingerprinting system gives you a position. This research adds scan-level evidence for judging how well the Wi-Fi observations and radio-map matches support that position.

Explore real scan evidence Get started with real data Understand the idea

Research implementation · Python and Android Java · Reproducible data and source

docs.title: The idea in one diagram
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Wi-Fi query scan] --> C[Compare fingerprints]
    B[Radio map: RSS and known positions] --> C
    C --> D[Candidate reference points]
    D --> E[Position estimate]
    D --> F[Scan-level indicators]
    A --> F
    F --> G[Five SQS components]
    G --> H[SQS and diagnostics]
    E --> I[Position + reliability evidence]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Inspect or apply a calibrated decision rule]

A score is not a certainty

The Scan Quality and Support Score (SQS) summarizes support from the recorded scan and radio map. It is not a calibrated probability that an estimated position is correct. A decision threshold must be fitted and evaluated separately.

docs.title: Android implementation
docs.text: The Java application performs Wi-Fi scan inspection, floor inference, WKNN positioning, and scan-level diagnostic presentation. The public project contains source and an empty schema, with no private radio-map database or Block Z floor plans.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
The source declares Android Gradle Plugin 8.13.0, Gradle 8.13, JDK 17, compile/target SDK 35, and minimum API 26. These Gradle/JDK/build-tools requirements follow the official AGP 8.13 compatibility table.

Open android/ in Android Studio, install SDK 35 and Build Tools 35.0.0, then run:

cd android
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug
# Windows: gradlew.bat testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug

The included wrapper uses the official distribution checksum. APKs, build outputs, local SDK paths, signing files, and scan histories are not committed. See the current integration validation report for independent checks and limitations.

docs.title: First launch and local data
docs.text:
The app creates an empty SQLite database from app/src/main/assets/database/schema.sql. Import an authorized local radio-map package through the Radio Maps screen using IMPORT_FORMAT.md. No default private building or floor is selected in source.

The fabricated AP tokens in the public synthetic fixture cannot identify live access points and are not a replacement for an authorized local radio-map import. Imported calibrations must match the selected floor, WKNN setting, and diagnostic candidate count. Missing calibration leaves raw diagnostics available without pretending that calibrated warning outputs exist.

CALIBRATION.md defines the independent-reference/held-out protocol. Imported profile provenance must be retained separately; Android's CSV importer alone does not prove independent calibration.

docs.title: Interpretation of the 99-run timing experiment
docs.text:
The historical record describes 99 runs and an indicator/composite/warning computation median of approximately 0.43 ms. This source release does not independently verify the recorded device metadata or original 99 raw timings.

That interval begins after candidate retrieval and coordinate estimation. It excludes Wi-Fi acquisition, floor inference, radio-map loading, fingerprint preparation, candidate retrieval, coordinate estimation, rendering, and persistence. It is a computational-cost measurement, not an end-to-end latency benchmark, accuracy test, or independent live warning-effectiveness evaluation. These historical device measurements have not been newly repeated as part of the repository build checks.

docs.title: Android scope and 99-run measurement
docs.text:
The reported 99-run Android experiment addresses only the computational cost of 18 retained indicator calculations, three composite outputs included therein, and adverse-percentile warning states after diagnostic candidates and coordinate estimates are already available. In the code, distinguish the candidateRetrievalMs, positionEstimationMs, indicatorComputationMs, and any UI/export/total elapsed figures.

Do not label indicator computation cost as end-to-end scan-to-position latency, or reinterpret repeated runtime measurements as an experiment on diagnosis accuracy, classification precision, cross-dataset effectiveness, or floor-detection correctness. Keep the phone model, Android version, CPU state, thermal controls, raw 99 values (if releasable), timing statistic, and source commit alongside any reproduced number. This local candidate contains the timing source and column definitions; the original on-device 99-run raw record and a fresh build are not asserted here.

docs.title: What the historical results establish
docs.text:
Historical analyses use cohort-relative indicator scaling and ranks to study associations and gross-error discrimination. When a distribution is derived from the evaluated cohort, its results are retrospective. It must not be described as an independently fitted online calibration or as prospective warning performance.

The Android implementation can apply condition-specific reference distributions. The reported live timing measurements demonstrate the cost of indicator/composite/warning computation. They do not establish the statistical adequacy or independent predictive effectiveness of an imported profile.

docs.title: Protocol for prospective use
docs.text:
1. Freeze the radio map, training AP vocabulary, positioning estimator and its settings, and diagnostic candidate count (M = 10).
  2. Collect a separate calibration cohort representative of the intended condition. Keep the final evaluation cohort separate; account for repeated locations, sessions, and devices when designing the split.
  3. Fit the 5th/95th percentile scaling bounds and empirical distributions of the 15 individual indicators on calibration data only.
  4. Construct SQS, Cσ, and FII with those frozen bounds. Fit the three composite reference distributions on the resulting calibration scores.
  5. Freeze a versioned profile with its cohort identity, floor, estimator, sample counts, and provenance. Apply it unchanged to held-out evaluation scans.
  6. Evaluate warning behavior against held-out outcomes. Any recalibration creates a new profile and requires a new evaluation; query observations must not silently alter the existing reference.

The included Python builder checks disjoint scan IDs, explicit profile roles, and condition identity. ID disjointness alone cannot prove session/location independence or representativeness. The minimum of eight finite records is an input guard, not a claim that eight scans are adequate for calibration.

docs.title: Adverse percentile and cutoff
docs.text:
For a reference set of size n, adverse percentile is:

  • High-is-adverse: count(reference <= observed) / n.
  • Low-is-adverse: count(reference >= observed) / n.

Ties are inclusive. A warning is raised at adverse percentile ≥ 0.80. Ties can make the actual warning rate differ from 20%. These percentiles express condition-relative extremeness; neither they nor SQS are calibrated probabilities of positioning failure. Missing indicator values must be shown as unavailable.

Composite scaling clips (value - q05) / (q95 - q05) to [0, 1]. The implementation uses the Android-compatible neutral value 0.5 for a degenerate scaling interval or missing scaling input; this fallback is not evidence of good support.

docs.title: Build a frozen profile
docs.text:
Prepare a local CSV containing scan_id and the 15 raw indicator columns, plus a separate CSV containing held-out scan_id values.

python scripts/build_calibration.py --input /private/calibration.csv --evaluation-ids /private/heldout_ids.csv --output /private/profiles/site_v1 --floor-id local_floor_1 --estimator WKNN-k3 --reference-id calibration_session_v1 --role calibration

Use the exact estimator identity expected by the Android importer. The command writes profile.json and calibration.csv, refuses to overwrite an existing profile, and records reference-value checksums. Keep both files locally together: the Android CSV alone does not carry all provenance fields.

--role retrospective explicitly labels a descriptive cohort profile. The Python online application function rejects retrospective roles and floor/estimator/M mismatches. The Android importer does not enforce the JSON provenance role; deployment owners must preserve and review that provenance themselves. No generic calibration fallback or independent deployment performance is claimed.

Without a matching imported calibration, Android still supports available raw diagnostics. Calibrated composites and warning percentiles remain unavailable. See the Android import format.

docs.title: ESWA R3 reproducibility and interpretation audit
docs.text:
R3 issue Evidence present Remaining limitation Replace repository placeholder and verify accessibility The GitHub repository exists and its link can be verified; this local package contains a reproducible scalar-reference analyzer Candidate is not yet uploaded/approved; public links in manuscript must match actually released files Warning calibration Java percentile direction/ties/0.80 cutoff and an explicit split-isolation script; docs/WARNING_CALIBRATION.md Retrospective study references must not be presented as prospective withheld calibration 99-run timing Java source and docs/ANDROID_TIMING.md record the exact post-candidate diagnostic computation boundary Device build/raw 99-run logfile still requires separate verification Cross-dataset robustness Per-query 10-unit, 8-estimator evaluation residuals and scale-free indicators Evidence limited to observed units, source conditions, estimators and the manuscript evaluation design

Original research package limitations found in the September audit: native SQS was different from frozen reference on 8,166 of 13,629 rows (max difference ≈0.194591); stored-feature arithmetic reconstruction was exact, but no causal explanation of native discrepancies was established. Native AP-token Transformer and residual CNN adapters were missing, while frozen predictions exist for all eight estimators. CatBoost preprocessing/hyperparameter equivalence remains unverified. The SQS-only case explorer differs from the manuscript's eight-indicator confidence rule. These are not repaired or silently declared resolved here.

Source-scan licensing, archive DOI, software license, exact private calibration-input identity, compiled Android build and full end-to-end regeneration are not asserted. Do not upload the manuscript or sensitive floor-plan sources.

docs.title: Obtaining and formatting the ten empirical evaluation units
docs.text: This guide is for executing the existing Wi-Fi fingerprinting estimators, scan-level reliability code, and research analysis. The public repository contains measured UJIIndoorLoc units U01–U03 and measured HK U09. For U04–U08 and U10, use the dataset publishers' download pages below and prepare the input locally. The publisher datasets have their own licenses and attribution requirements; their files are not relicensed under this repository's MIT code license.

The research uses its own preprocessing and train/test partitions. A user's new partition from the same published source should not be presented as the identical paper experiment.

docs.title: 2. Required canonical file format
docs.text:
Save each separately authorized unit as LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS/U04.csv.gz (replace U04 with its unit ID). The file must be a gzip-compressed UTF-8 CSV with exactly these eight columns in this order:

dataset,group,split,row_id,floor,x,y,rss_json

Example fabricated rows for unit U04:

dataset,group,split,row_id,floor,x,y,rss_json
TUT_WLAN_RSS_1161525,TUT,train,U04-train-000000,0,12.50,7.00,"{""AP1"":-63.0,""AP4"":-80.0}"
TUT_WLAN_RSS_1161525,TUT,test,U04-test-000000,0,13.00,8.25,"{""AP1"":-66.0,""AP4"":-78.0}"

Rules:

  1. dataset and group must match the corresponding strings in config/datasets.yaml. For U09, the existing public HK_U09 / HK_LOCAL aliases are also accepted by the input stager.
  2. split must be train (radio-map fingerprints with reference locations) or test (held-out scans with ground-truth locations for retrospective scoring). Preserve the study-specific assignments when seeking manuscript equivalence.
  3. row_id must be unique within a unit; identifiers must not expose source participants or hardware IDs. Preserve test-row ordering when aligning existing paper predictions.
  4. floor is a categorical integer, such as 0, 1, 2. Do not treat it as a floor height. If source floors are unavailable (U10), use -1 consistently.
  5. x, y are finite local metric positions, in metres, with the same origin, scale and axes across training and test rows of that unit. Translating all positions by one common offset changes no 2D error or distance; do not independently shift train and test sets. Keep each unit's coordinate frame separate.
  6. rss_json is an escaped JSON object of AP labels to observed RSSI in dBm. Use AP1, AP2, ... consistently across all scans within the same unit. If a signal is unobserved, omit that AP; do not place 100 or 0 as a fake measurement. The source-specific +100 missing sentinel should be removed. Do not mix units' AP namespaces or publish real MAC addresses, SSIDs or router names.
  7. A .csv.gz may be read with pandas.read_csv or Python gzip.open. No floor-plan image, building vector, geodetic coordinate origin, inverse AP-to-BSSID mapping, or real SSID is necessary.

docs.title: 3. Transforming original publisher files
docs.text:
Download and extract the indicated source into an external local folder. Prepare one source unit at a time, using the publisher's own measurement/coordinate files:

  • UJIIndoorLoc, U01–U03: The original files contain WAP001–WAP520, LONGITUDE, LATITUDE, FLOOR, BUILDINGID. Group building IDs 0, 1 and 2 separately. The UCI trainingData.csv and validationData.csv provide an official split, not the independent ESWA 80/20 study split. The already released U01–U03 files supply the study-derived partitions.
  • TUT WLAN, U04: Pair each Training_rss.csv row to the same row in Training_coordinates.csv; repeat for the corresponding Test_*.csv files. The source provides 3D location data and uses 100 as an unobserved-signal marker. The ESWA count is not the same as the original publisher split.
  • TAU U05–U06: In each building folder, pair rm_rss.csv with rm_crd.csv by row number for the radio map; pair the equivalent eval_* files for queries. Both have metric XY positions and floor IDs. Missing RSS values use +100 in the original.
  • Tampere U07–U08: In each of SAH1 and TIE1, match *_training_rss.csv and *_training_coordinates.csv by row, likewise *_test_* files. The publisher's tests have different sizes from the manuscript's derived splits; preserve the study splits if exact comparison is required.
  • DSI U10: Read the source radio-map and evaluation files from the Zenodo archive; inspect the original columns and measurement convention before selecting XY, APs and any floor code. In the ESWA registry, U10 has no floor ground truth: set floor=-1. Keep the publisher observations and document your split.

For both a simple wide RSS table and the publisher's paired RSS/coordinates files, use scripts/import_external_unit.py (usage below). It converts columns to a single stable AP namespace and writes the eight-column format; it does not reproduce an unpublished study-specific split. If source RSS and coordinates are in separate files, inspect and set --floor-index correctly for the particular archive.

# Example: original TUT train/test RSS and coordinate files (choose the
# actual floor column index by examining the downloaded CSV files).
python scripts/import_external_unit.py --unit U04 --mode paired \
  --train-rss /datasets/TUT/Training_rss.csv \
  --train-coords /datasets/TUT/Training_coordinates.csv \
  --test-rss /datasets/TUT/Test_rss.csv \
  --test-coords /datasets/TUT/Test_coordinates.csv \
  --floor-index 2 --output-dir LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS

# Example: official wide UJI sources, building 0 (not the paper split).
python scripts/import_external_unit.py --unit U01 --mode wide \
  --train /datasets/UJI/trainingData.csv --test /datasets/UJI/validationData.csv \
  --x-column LONGITUDE --y-column LATITUDE --floor-column FLOOR \
  --building-column BUILDINGID --building-value 0 --ap-prefix WAP \
  --output-dir LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS

The converter does not rescale RSS or positions, estimate missing floor labels, infer unknown file headers, or determine a manuscript's held-out scans. Select the correct columns based on each original dataset's documentation.

docs.title: 4. Preparing matrices and executing code
docs.text:
python -m pip install -e ".[dev,empirical]"
python scripts/validate_uji_release.py
# Prepare the publicly included UJI study units:
python scripts/stage_existing_units.py --input-dir data/empirical --units U01 U02 U03
# Prepare an externally downloaded/transformed unit while accepting an
# independently chosen split different from the paper:
python scripts/stage_existing_units.py --input-dir LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS --units U04 --allow-custom-splits
# For an exact study-derived unit, omit --allow-custom-splits:
python scripts/stage_existing_units.py --input-dir LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS --units U04

This produces data/processed/units/U04/radio_map_matrices.npz, ap_vocabulary_train.json, and scan_metadata.csv.gz using the existing original harmonization functions. The corresponding existing estimator code can then be invoked (example):

python -m wifi_integrity benchmark-native --units U04 --estimators knn,wknn --output-name u04_native.csv.gz

Historical experimental outputs in results/approved/ and results/empirical/hk_u09/ are archived results and are not overwritten by this pipeline. For reproducible comparisons, keep source download/version, choices of columns, transformations, split membership, AP mapping, software versions and random seeds.

docs.title: 5. Data rights and scientific reproducibility
docs.text: UJIIndoorLoc's CC BY 4.0 explicitly allows redistribution with credit. For the other publishers, their source records are linked above; publicly available files do not by themselves establish that this repository may rehost modified copies. Readers should download directly and follow each publisher's terms. Different source versions, user-defined splits or preprocessing may produce different numbers from the ESWA reference results.

docs.title: Data provenance
docs.text:
examples/synthetic_combined/ remains the fully synthetic ten-unit software-test dataset.

data/empirical/hk_u09_ap_relative.csv.gz contains real HK RSS fingerprints: 4,150 scans (3,319 training; 831 test), 11 floor categories and 525 APs renamed AP1 through AP525. It uses relative metre coordinates and retains measured RSS and split memberships, while source BSSIDs, MAC addresses, SSIDs, router names, original scan IDs, coordinate origin and real map image/vector assets are absent. These are not synthetic observations, and the relative point arrangement has not been removed.

Its CSV schema is dataset,group,split,row_id,floor,x,y,rss_json with local dataset label HK_U09. Validate via python scripts/validate_hk_empirical.py. HK U09 and CC BY-licensed UJIIndoorLoc U01–U03 are distributed as measured inputs. The other six units U04–U08 and U10 have official publisher download pages in docs/DATASET_DOWNLOADS_AND_FORMAT.md; their derived harmonized files are not redistributed here. MIT is a software/synthetic license and does not automatically establish reuse rights in third-party empirical measurements.

docs.title: Native positioning estimators
docs.text:
CLI identifier Estimator Dependency knn K-nearest neighbors Core wknn Weighted K-nearest neighbors Core random_forest Random forest Core extra_trees Extra trees Core hgb Histogram-based gradient boosting Core catboost CatBoost multi-output regression catboost extra transformer_ap AP-token Transformer transformer extra residual_cnn Residual CNN cnn extra 
python -m pip install -e ".[dev,catboost,transformer,cnn]"
python scripts/check_native_estimators.py --require-all
python scripts/prepare_hk_data.py
python -m wifi_integrity benchmark-native --units U09 --estimators catboost,transformer_ap,residual_cnn

The smoke command fits all eight adapters on a small synthetic problem. Neural adapters run only two epochs in this check; this establishes executable fit/inference paths, not scientific accuracy.

The neural training functions were recovered from the original source workspace. The public adapters retain their training logic and return fitted models and training-only transforms for separate inference. AP-token defaults are 128 selected APs, 60 maximum epochs, batch size 256, and seed 42. The residual CNN uses the recovered residual architecture, train-only standardization, and a training/validation partition for early stopping. Source hashes and adaptations are recorded in metadata/source_provenance.json.

The CatBoost adapter selects up to 128 APs using training observation frequency/variance, supplies RSS and observation-mask features, uses a 15% training-validation split, and defaults to 800 iterations, depth 6, learning rate 0.05, and seed 42. KNN/WKNN settings are read from the stored per-unit study estimator names.

Fresh outputs go to results/predictions/estimator_predictions_native.csv.gz. They are kept distinct from reference predictions. Exact historical equality is not promised for all estimators or environments. The validation record states which native experiments were actually run.

docs.title: Existing measured inputs, radio map and historical results
docs.text: The repository already contains the original Python indicator, SQS, estimator, analysis and Android application source. This addition does not invent or re-run the historical experiments. It supplies their existing HK U09 inputs and approved outputs in a consistent, origin-free coordinate frame.

docs.title: Where to find the files
docs.text:
• data/empirical/hk_u09_ap_relative.csv.gz: previously published measured U09 input (3,319 train; 831 test). Its rows were shuffled on release and reidentified, so do not join by its public HK_SCAN_* identifiers.
  • data/radio_maps/hk_u09_train.csv.gz: the same 3,319 training measurements, preserved in source order, with AP1...AP525 and relative coordinates. This is the fingerprint radio map, not a floor-plan image.
  • data/empirical/hk_u09_test_ordered.csv.gz: the same 831 test measurements in original evaluation order, with U09-test-000000 through U09-test-000830. It makes joining the preexisting results unambiguous.
  • results/empirical/hk_u09/historical_estimator_predictions.csv.gz: 6,648 saved original predictions, 8 estimators × 831 queries, not baseline retraining.
  • results/empirical/hk_u09/historical_scan_reliability.csv.gz: 831 original indicator and SQS records.
  • results/empirical/hk_u09/historical_reliability_decisions.csv.gz: 6,648 original per-estimator reliability and gross-error decision records.
  • results/approved/: original approved experimental aggregate summaries for the ten-unit study, including SQS ablations, association/CI, gross-error results, floor-aware validation, warning sensitivity and runtime. These are stored outputs, not rerun experiments.

A single fixed local-origin translation has been applied consistently. The original coordinate origin is not distributed. This translation preserves pairwise distances and horizontal positioning errors. Original per-estimator coordinate rounding differs by up to 0.03 m for some methods. These historical values are deliberately preserved rather than forcibly replaced with more precise input coordinates.

docs.title: Verify original outputs
docs.text:
python scripts/verify_existing_research_assets.py

This performs bytewise checksums, dataset count/identity checks, cross-file scan-index matching and coordinate/error invariance checks. It does not claim to retrain all eight historical estimators or regenerate the original indicators from scratch.

To recompute a separate new KNN/WKNN/Random Forest baseline from measured U09 data:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev,empirical]"
python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode hk-u09

U01–U03 are included as measured UJIIndoorLoc study units under CC BY 4.0 with attribution. U04–U08 and U10 have original publisher download links and a formatting guide at docs/DATASET_DOWNLOADS_AND_FORMAT.md; their harmonized empirical copies are not hosted in this repository. Original floor-plan images and vectors are never supplied.

docs.title: Getting started with the public fixture
docs.text:
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m pytest -q
python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode demo
python scripts/validate_synthetic_combined.py

The fabricated ten-unit input is examples/synthetic_combined/combined_all_datasets.csv.gz. It is not anonymized empirical data. To prepare a local processing workspace, run:

python scripts/prepare_research_workspace.py --combined examples/synthetic_combined/combined_all_datasets.csv.gz

Private empirical study references are not included. scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode reference needs authorized reference files and cannot run by default.

docs.title: HK building-data and reproducibility release boundary (ESWA R3)
docs.text: This policy applies to the public GitHub source candidate and any future pull request, release archive, dashboard payload, or test fixture. The repository is not yet published as a completed reproducibility package.

docs.title: Hard exclusions
docs.text:
• No HK building floor-plan images or recreations: no PNG/JPEG/PDF maps, stitched screenshots, scans, and no traced/embedded SVG, CAD, GIS, DXF, vector PDFs, GeoJSON polygons, path descriptions, SVG strings or HTML/JS canvas representations containing identifiable HK floor geometry.
  • No real HK access-point identifiers, including BSSID/MAC addresses, SSIDs, AP-to-floor lookup tables, ordered AP identifiers that can be linked back to the HK system, fingerprints or raw Wi-Fi captures. Java code implementing the BSSID interface may be released without any observational values.
  • No absolute site coordinates or georeferences: no latitude/longitude, projected eastings/northings, per-floor origins, coordinate transform back to a true survey frame, surveyed floor footprints or actual reference-point clouds.
  • No trajectory/map reconstruction through indirect means: even origin-shifted HK RP coordinates, dense query coordinates, ordered tracks, heat maps, vector figures, candidate scatter diagrams, and derived raster grids are blocked from the public release unless a separate disclosure review expressly approves them.

docs.title: Data representation
docs.text:
The source-only public candidate uses (1) fully synthetic local XY examples and dummy, locally administered AP addresses, and (2) condition-level scalar summaries with pseudonymous unit labels. The real HK radio maps, scans, positions, and research floor geometry are not present.

The separately held full scalar-review ZIP contains per-query indicator values and estimator error-vector residuals, subject to dataset-derivative sharing permission. For a private local-metric observation with ground truth g=(gx,gy) and estimator output p=(px,py), define:

delta_x = px - gx, delta_y = py - gy, error_2d = sqrt(delta_x**2 + delta_y**2).

If an internal local origin o is used, p_local = p - o and g_local = g - o, but their difference is unchanged: (p-o) - (g-o) = p-g. The public release must not include either actual p_local or g_local for HK; it may use approved displacement errors or higher-level statistical aggregates. Merely subtracting an origin does not anonymize a recognizable building layout.

Use scripts/export_relative_errors.py only on private input files already expressed in consistent local metres. The script exports only pseudonymous IDs and relative residuals and does not write the input coordinate columns, BSSIDs, floor geometry, or reference origin. It does not establish legal permission to publish the output.

docs.title: Enforcement and review
docs.text:
• CI calls scripts/check_release_safety.py and tests/test_privacy_gate.py before the synthetic demonstration. They reject geo/vector/image files, disguised binary payloads, embedded floor maps, BSSID literals except four documented fictitious addresses in the synthetic importer demonstration, live research record CSVs, nonempty SQLite tables, altered Android vector XML, and unexpected local coordinate payloads.
  • The Android asset database in the public source contains an empty schema. The only XML vector drawable with a path is the hash-locked generic Wi-Fi app launcher icon. The legacy website includes one empty SVG plotting surface, not a map.
  • Avoid adding a new image or vector to the public source without an explicit inspection and approval, even when the file appears generic. External build artifacts, APKs, screenshots, manuscripts and supplementary materials are not included.
  • Before any upload, perform a clean-archive re-extraction, rerun privacy tests, review every new/changed asset manually, and obtain authorization for third-party derived datasets and code licensing. Git ignore rules are secondary; they do not prevent already-tracked or forced additions.

Do not upload the separate full scalar review ZIP to the public GitHub repository unless a new review and derivative-distribution authorization explicitly approve each table.

docs.title: Empirical HK U09: executable 2D positioning baseline
docs.text: The published input data/empirical/hk_u09_ap_relative.csv.gz contains 4,150 real observed HK Wi-Fi scans. It is not the ten-unit synthetic demonstration. Real BSSIDs and original scan identifiers are replaced with opaque AP labels and release scan IDs; coordinates are in local metres with no absolute origin. RSS observations and the existing 3,319/831 training/query split are preserved.

docs.title: One-command reproduction
docs.text:
At the repository root after python -m pip install -e ".[dev,empirical]":

python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode hk-u09
# Or run the native estimator driver directly:
python scripts/evaluate_hk_u09.py --check-frozen
# To save per-scan predictions locally (not tracked by Git):
python scripts/evaluate_hk_u09.py --save-predictions

Outputs: results/empirical/hk_u09/summary.json; optional predictions.csv.gz. --check-frozen compares specified output summaries with docs/hk_u09_expected_summary.json, with an absolute 0.03 m numerical tolerance for possible dependency changes. CI reruns the baseline and checks the input SHA-256. The frozen numerical results use NumPy 2.3.5, pandas 2.2.3 and scikit-learn 1.8.0 via .[empirical]; versions are checked explicitly rather than silently changing the reference.

docs.title: Explicit protocol
docs.text:
• Models: existing repository RetrievalEstimator for KNN and WKNN, and make_random_forest for RF. No additional independent estimator source is used.
  • KNN and WKNN: k=5, Euclidean distance on the existing legacy feature interface (0 for unobserved APs). WKNN uses power=2. RF: 80 trees, maximum depth 18, minimum leaf 2, max_features=sqrt; seed=42.
  • AP vocabulary learned exclusively from training RSS. Train=3,319, test=831, features=525. No test labels are used in training, feature selection, or estimator settings. No hyperparameter tuning was done on the held-out test set.
  • All models are floor-agnostic and return only (x,y). True floors are not available to the estimators; wrong-floor detection and 3D positioning are not evaluated. Error is Euclidean 2D distance in relative metres.
  • Input checksum: b99bac3454e8f0f306c7fb8c012a7def5e277251c8013304e50e02ae51717078.

docs.title: Independently executed results on the released U09 table
docs.text:
Estimator Mean error (m) Median (m) P90 (m) P95 (m) RMSE (m) KNN 4.3766 3.4504 9.1161 10.6208 5.7524 WKNN 4.1537 3.2395 8.6327 10.2415 5.4854 Random Forest 6.3518 5.0559 11.9108 16.1534 8.3550

This is a new reproducible empirical baseline and not a reconstruction of the paper's original tuning or eight-estimator evaluation; it does not establish equivalence with published results. The 831 query scans should not be treated as 831 statistically independent trajectory trials because observations may be spatially correlated. No inference about calibration, gross-error warning validity, or cross-dataset performance follows from these numbers. The other nine empirical units and the original reference outputs remain outside this public evaluation.

Documentation home · Research overview

docs.title: SQS and warning interpretation
docs.text:
SQS combines signal support, candidate-geometry support, AP-count support, AP-overlap support, and local-density support. Its nominal component weights are equal. It summarizes diagnostic support; it is not a learned error predictor or a calibrated probability.

A condition-relative adverse percentile describes the position of an indicator within a reference distribution. The reference population, fitted scaling, unavailable-value policy, and warning threshold must be stated when interpreting a score or moving from offline analysis to new live scans.

RSS standard deviation and RSS range do not consistently follow their prespecified adverse directions in the current study. Their configuration signs must not be presented as universal reliability rules. Similarly, favorable RSS matching alone does not establish that candidate locations are spatially coherent.

docs.title: Recompute scan-level reliability using the public empirical data
docs.text: The public repository includes four measured empirical units, U01–U03 (UJIIndoorLoc, 3 buildings) and U09 (Hong Kong), plus source code for the original scan-level reliability computation and SQS. The demonstration below uses the same wifi_integrity.reliability.indicators._unit_features and reconstruct_sqs implementations as the existing research source; it does not replace them with new algorithms.

docs.title: One command from measured input to native output
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev,empirical]"
python scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py

To run only HK U09 (also exercised by GitHub Actions):

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py --units U09
python scripts/check_public_integrity_release.py --check-fresh

The script reads data/empirical/U01.csv.gz, U02.csv.gz and U03.csv.gz; for U09, it reads the original-order data/radio_maps/hk_u09_train.csv.gz and data/empirical/hk_u09_test_ordered.csv.gz, not the separately shuffled HK demonstration table. It validates the expected original study counts and retained scan IDs, and calls the existing original reliability implementation without retraining estimators.

Outputs are written under the locally ignored results/public_integrity/ directory:

  • Uxx_scan_reliability.csv.gz: per-query diagnostic indicators, three composites (SQS, C_sigma, FII), diagnostic coordinates, relative ground-truth coordinates and scan identifiers.
  • Uxx_retrieved_candidates.csv.gz: ten nearest diagnostic radio-map candidates for each test scan, using local relative metric coordinates.
  • summary.json: number of processed records, average/median SQS and source file hashes.

Frozen examples of these freshly computed outputs are committed to examples/empirical_integrity/ so that users can inspect the results without rerunning the algorithm.

docs.title: Verification against committed outputs
docs.text:
python scripts/check_public_integrity_release.py

This checks all 5,041 stored scan-feature rows and 50,410 candidate rows, scan key alignment, rank completeness and exact SQS reconstruction. The optional --check-fresh matches all 831 U09 scan IDs and compares mean and median SQS with a tolerance of 0.001 on the unit interval. It reports the maximum and mean absolute per-scan differences instead of claiming bit-for-bit identity across different NumPy/BLAS environments. The source implementation's float32 nearest-candidate selection can differ at near-ties even with single-thread execution. Original historical outputs remain unchanged.

Unit Training RSS scans Test scans Candidate rows U01 4,628 1,157 11,570 U02 4,402 1,101 11,010 U03 7,808 1,952 19,520 U09 3,319 831 8,310 Total 20,157 5,041 50,410

Distinguish three kinds of output. (1) These files are new native computations from the released measurements. (2) results/empirical/hk_u09/historical_*.csv.gz contain the stored original eight-estimator and scan-level results. (3) results/approved/ contains approved original ten-unit aggregate summaries. The new computations are not guaranteed to equal the archived historical outputs because candidate tie handling, source ordering, numerical environment and preprocessing may differ. No historical output has been overwritten.

SQS uses cohort-relative scaling in the current implementation. This retrospective execution is not an independently calibrated online reliability guarantee, and the command does not retrain all eight historical models or measure prospective gross-error-warning performance.

For the remaining six dataset units, consult official dataset downloads and the required local input format. To reproduce an exact study experiment, retain its original split and preprocessing decisions.

docs.title: Reproducibility and evidence limits
docs.text:
Four distinct execution routes must not be conflated:

  1. Public synthetic demonstration: python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode demo; python scripts/validate_synthetic_combined.py. These test packaging, I/O, estimator invocation and synthetic source-to-output operations only.
  2. Public empirical HK U09 baseline: python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode hk-u09 trains the existing KNN, WKNN and Random Forest implementations on 3,319 observed training scans, then evaluates 831 held-out scans. See docs/HK_U09_EMPIRICAL_REPRODUCIBILITY.md. This is a new baseline, not the historical eight-estimator study replay.
  3. Private empirical reference replay: python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode reference; this requires separately authorized reference/approved/legacy_canonical/ records, intentionally absent from the public archive. Reference replay recomputes output statistics from historical features/predictions, not model retraining.
  4. Full native empirical pipeline: requires the original study datasets and precise split/protocol controls. These data and complete historical run artifacts are not distributed here. A run on the synthetic fixture cannot reproduce reported study positioning accuracy or warnings.

tests/unit/ run in the public checkout. tests/reference/ need generated products or separately supplied research assets. The default pytest configuration runs only public-safe unit tests; the reference suite is not claimed to pass without those inputs.

Historical timing: the 99-run Android result concerns post-retrieval indicator/composite/warning computation, excluding scan capture and positioning stages. Cohort-relative adverse percentile thresholds do not establish prospective warning calibration; deployable cutoffs need a separate fixed calibration cohort and independent evaluation. Cross-dataset robustness is limited to the evaluated dataset units and estimators.

docs.title: External measured dataset inputs
docs.text: See dataset download links and canonical input format. scripts/import_external_unit.py adapts wide or paired Wi-Fi RSS files, and scripts/stage_existing_units.py prepares radio-map matrices with the original repository code. New partitions should not be equated with the study's archived numerical results.

docs.title: Fresh empirical scan-level reliability outputs on public units
docs.text: The original indicator and SQS implementations can now be executed directly using measured UJIIndoorLoc U01–U03 and anonymous HK U09 RSS tables: python scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py. The frozen new results (5,041 scan records and 50,410 candidate records) are under examples/empirical_integrity/. Execute python scripts/check_public_integrity_release.py to validate their row identities and arithmetic. These results are not a replacement for the original paper's eight-estimator retrospective tables. See docs/PUBLIC_EMPIRICAL_INTEGRITY.md.

docs.title: Research overview
docs.text:
The framework examines whether scan-level observations and radio-map support can help diagnose unreliable Wi-Fi fingerprinting estimates. Its evidence covers 10 retained dataset units, 54,520 training scans, 13,629 query scans, and eight positioning estimators.

The 18 diagnostics combine scan statistics, radio-map compatibility, local spatial support, candidate geometry, map ambiguity, and three composite scores. SQS uses equally weighted signal, geometry, AP-count, overlap, and density support. It is an interpretable summary, not a learned probability of correctness.

The analyses examine indicator–error associations, discrimination of adaptive and fixed-threshold gross errors, SQS components and ablations, unit-cluster uncertainty, floor-aware behavior, sensitivity, runtime, and confidently wrong fixes.

Interpretation is bounded by the evaluated units, splits, estimator settings, and acquisition conditions. Cross-dataset consistency does not establish invariance to arbitrary buildings or devices. Auxiliary floor inference is not a general vertical-positioning guarantee. Strong nominal RSS matching does not guarantee spatial coherence or low position error.

Historical cohort-relative analysis, independent prospective calibration, fresh estimator training, stored-reference checks, and device runtime measurements answer different questions. The reproducibility guide and calibration protocol keep these distinctions explicit.

docs.title: Availability and next stages
docs.text:
Stage Current status Next evidence needed Runnable Python package Included with demo, eight native adapters, and unit tests Extend checks to additional supported environments Reference reproducibility Included numerical checks, ablations, and unit-cluster intervals Independently reproduce full historical training where source data are authorized HK public data Relative locations and opaque AP tokens included Maintain privacy review for future additions Android source Included with empty database initialization and local import Validate on additional devices and authorized radio maps Prospective warning evaluation Frozen-profile tooling and protocol included Independent calibration/evaluation cohorts and reported effectiveness Extended raw-data analyses Original numerical drivers included with prerequisites Acquire authorized third-party radio maps and run the full experiments

Future data or result additions must preserve the publication boundaries in DATA_AND_PRIVACY.md. The current package does not include the manuscript, private floor maps, or private identifier mappings.

docs.title: Running the original ESWA ten-unit source with measured inputs
docs.text: The repository contains the original implementation of the estimators, 18 selected scan-level indicators, composite SQS, retrospective warning analysis and supplementary analysis drivers. The approved reference outputs are archived and not rebuilt by the input-preparation command.

docs.title: Available measurement data
docs.text:
• U01–U03: transformed subsets of UJIIndoorLoc, with source attribution and CC BY 4.0 reuse notice in docs/UJI_DATA_ATTRIBUTION.md. The data/empirical/U0*.csv.gz files include observed train and test RSS; split=train rows are the radio map.
  • U09: observed HK U09 with AP1, ... identifiers and relative metre coordinates, already published at data/empirical/hk_u09_ap_relative.csv.gz. Ordered input for the original results is separately available in data/radio_maps/hk_u09_train.csv.gz and data/empirical/hk_u09_test_ordered.csv.gz.
  • U04–U08 and U10: original measurement sources at the dataset publisher pages; the curated, identifier-relabeled combined unit tables are supplied only in the local full research bundle until applicable redistribution conditions have been checked. They are not generated by a synthetic fixture.

docs.title: Reproducing with all ten authorized input tables
docs.text:
From the full local research bundle (or a GitHub clone with ten compatible authorized files copied into an ignored local LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS/ directory):

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python scripts/stage_existing_units.py --input-dir ../LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS
python -m wifi_integrity benchmark-native --units U10 --estimators knn,wknn --output-name u10_native.csv.gz
python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode reference
python scripts/verify_existing_research_assets.py
  • stage_existing_units.py validates original 54,520 training and 13,629 test scan counts; produces data/processed/units/Uxx/radio_map_matrices.npz and AP vocabularies using existing repository harmonization functions. No fitting or experimental result substitution occurs at this stage.
  • benchmark-native runs source estimators with a fresh fit, saving predictions and numerical summaries under results/ (locally ignored). Other estimator IDs in the existing code are random_forest, extra_trees, hgb, catboost, transformer_ap, residual_cnn. Install optional backend dependencies for the latter three. Fresh estimators are not guaranteed to match the historically approved model fit and tuning; the original stored results remain the reference.
  • reproduce_release.py --mode reference replays approved stored predictions and the numerical indicator/diagnostic analysis. It does not retrain all eight estimators. The appropriate input reference data live in reference/approved/legacy_canonical/ in the full local source package.
  • The source code uses the original saved estimator configurations as appropriate. To make a full comparison to the paper, inspect config/estimators.yaml and the source’s native estimator parameter derivation, then compare unit/condition outputs to the approved references, rather than claiming equality without testing.

docs.title: UJIIndoorLoc empirical data attribution and modification notice
docs.text:
Original dataset: Joaquín Torres-Sospedra, Raúl Montoliu, Adolfo Martínez-Usó, Tomás Arnau and Joan Avariento. UJIIndoorLoc, UCI Machine Learning Repository (2014). DOI: https://doi.org/10.24432/C5MS59.

Source and license: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/310/ujiindoorloc; Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.

This repository's changes: Three building-level evaluation units (U01–U03) have been selected from the existing harmonized ESWA research workspace; each retains its study training and test partitions and observed RSS values. AP columns/identifiers were relabeled to the stable anonymous AP1, AP2, ... namespace, spatial coordinates were expressed in a local-relative metric frame, and rows were serialized as gzipped CSV with sparse rss_json dictionaries and source-independent scan keys. The submitted study uses unit-specific splits, not necessarily the official source train/validation split. The transformed versions are not endorsed by the original dataset authors.

Only the derived dataset files are licensed under the terms applicable to UJIIndoorLoc; they are not part of the software MIT license. Keep this notice when redistributing the data.

docs.title: Adverse-percentile warnings: calibration boundary
docs.text:
The Inspector v1.0.9 DiagnosticEngine computes each raw indicator first, then (when an exact floor/estimator calibration exists) maps its value to an adverse percentile using a sorted reference distribution. For sorted values (r_1,...,r_n):

  • adverse high: count(r <= observed) / n (inclusive upper-tail rank in code terminology);
  • adverse low: count(r >= observed) / n (inclusive lower-tail rank);
  • warning when the resulting adverse fraction is >= 0.80.

Ties are handled by inclusive comparisons; the code uses upperBound for adverse-high and lowerBound for adverse-low. A warning is not a validated probability of positioning error, and when a matching profile is absent the warning count is unavailable rather than silently calibrated from another floor or estimator.

Retrospective results: calibration reference distributions formed from the analyzed study population summarize that population. They should not be characterized as fitted exclusively before its held-out evaluation unless that separation is documented.

Prospective application: to apply the procedure to a new scan, acquire a separate training/development/calibration population for the exact configured estimator/floor, fit the ordered reference distributions and required SQS scaling parameters without the held-out query, freeze the resulting artifact, and then evaluate queries only against those frozen values. Sensor scan observations themselves do not supply unknown GT errors; any choice of calibration populations must be explicit.

scripts/calibrate_warning_states.py is a separate executable split-isolated illustrative procedure. It rejects overlapping calibration/evaluation identifiers, records its calibration input hash, and does not claim that its quantiles reconstruct the original retrospective manuscript statistics.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text:
What is Wi-Fi fingerprinting?

It estimates a location by comparing observed Wi-Fi signal strengths with a radio map collected at reference positions.

What is a radio map? Do I need a building floor plan?

A radio map is an RSS/position table, not an architectural map. No original HK floor-plan image or vector file is needed to run the released examples.

What does SQS mean?

The Scan Quality and Support Score combines five kinds of diagnostic support (signal match, candidate geometry, AP count, AP overlap and local density). It is not a calibrated probability of correctness.

Does a high SQS prove that a position is accurate?

No. Some strong-looking fingerprint matches can produce large errors. Use SQS as diagnostic evidence, and calibrate and evaluate any operational warning rule separately.

Do I need ten datasets just to try the method?

No. Four measured units, U01–U03 and U09, are included and runnable. Six further units link to official dataset publishers for local preparation.

What is the difference between newly computed and historical results?

The public runner computes fresh indicators from distributed measurements. Historical files contain stored predictions and analyses from the original experiment. See evidence types.

What if my input dataset has a different CSV layout?

Use scripts/import_external_unit.py and the dataset-format guide. A new split or different transformation will not automatically match the manuscript results.

Can I run the Android app immediately with my building?

The app builds from Java source, but initializes an empty database. Import a radio map you are authorized to use and review calibration as described in the Android guide.

Are all datasets under the MIT license?

No. MIT applies to original code and synthetic fixtures. The UJIIndoorLoc data are under their source CC BY 4.0 terms, and other data require checking the source publisher's terms.

Is there a hosted interactive results dashboard?

Yes, the interactive measured-scan explorer visualizes 88 selected query scans from the four available measured units. It uses the original computed indicator/SQS values. The separate dashboard/ is synthetic, and the original web/ research interface is not a complete public live-positioning service.

Still need help? Open a GitHub issue with the unit ID, command, error message and non-sensitive input schema.

docs.title: Explore one measured Wi-Fi scan interactively
docs.text:
Choose a measured query scan from UJIIndoorLoc (U01–U03) or the anonymous HK unit (U09). The viewer follows its recorded Wi-Fi observations → retrieved radio-map candidates → geometry diagnostics → five SQS components → interpretation.

The example values come directly from the public native integrity computation and are not synthetic. There are 22 deterministic SQS-spanning samples from each of the four units, drawn from 5,041 evaluated scans. The SQS components are computed from the full unit, following the original code, not normalized against the 22 displayed samples.

A teaching view, not a calibrated alarm system

The viewer does not assign warnings or estimate probabilities of correctness. The candidate centroid shown on the local-X/Y plot is a diagnostic summary, not a fitted positioning estimator output. Ground-truth locations can be revealed only for retrospective illustration. Candidate coordinates are relative metres, not a floor-plan image.

docs.title: How this interactive data is produced
docs.text:
The site includes only a compact deterministic subset of records; the full results stay available in the repository. Regenerate the identical browser data from the existing native Python outputs:

python scripts/export_interactive_examples.py
python scripts/export_interactive_examples.py --check

The exporter verifies that each displayed SQS equals the equal-weight average of the five values obtained from the existing robust_unit_scale implementation, using all held-out scans for each unit. No estimator training or original manuscript results are modified.

Next: Understand every indicator · Run all four units · What the archived evidence proves.

docs.title: Why inspect the reliability of a Wi-Fi position?
docs.text:
A smartphone can estimate an indoor position without GPS by comparing the strengths of nearby Wi-Fi signals with a previously collected radio map. The radio map contains Wi-Fi observations and known reference positions. A typical estimator returns a location, often summarized by its average error over many test scans.

But a single estimate can be unexpectedly wrong even when the average performance is acceptable. For a navigation or sensor-fusion system, the question is not only Where am I? but also What evidence supports this particular estimate?

docs.title: Two scans, one positioning system
docs.text:
Scan with stronger support Scan worth inspecting Observable access points Several known APs Few known APs Fingerprint similarity Closely matches stored fingerprints Poor or ambiguous matches Retrieved candidate positions Cluster reasonably together Scattered between different areas Interpretation More supporting evidence Less consistent supporting evidence

The examples are illustrative, not measured cases or a fixed warning rule. A signal match that looks convincing can still produce a large error.

docs.title: The extra layer this project provides
docs.text:
Wi-Fi scan and radio-map data are used to calculate 18 selected diagnostic quantities, including three composite indicators. The individual quantities describe signal observations, match quality, geometric support and ambiguity. Five support components are combined into a Scan Quality and Support Score (SQS).

flowchart TB
    S[Single Wi-Fi scan] --> P[Positioning system]
    S --> R[Scan-level reliability layer]
    M[Reference radio map] --> P
    M --> R
    P --> O[Estimated position]
    R --> Q[18 diagnostic quantities, including SQS]
    O --> I[Estimate with evidence]
    Q --> I

The scores can help inspect, rank, compare, or flag scans. They do not automatically justify deployment decisions, and an SQS value is not an error probability.

docs.title: Five SQS support components
docs.text:
1. Signal-match support: how compatible the scan appears with its best reference fingerprints.
  2. Candidate-geometry support: whether candidate reference positions form a coherent neighborhood.
  3. AP-count support: how much access-point evidence was observed.
  4. AP-overlap support: how well the observed access-point set overlaps the radio map.
  5. Local-density support: how well the retrieved neighborhood is supported by nearby reference points.

The documented SQS combines these five components with equal nominal weights and cohort-relative scaling. See the full indicator table for their scientific definitions and directional conventions.

Do not mistake high support for ground-truth correctness

The SQS is not a calibrated accuracy percentage, confidence interval, or guaranteed bound on positioning error. Gross-error classification requires the specified reference distribution and evaluation protocol.

Next: Follow the pipeline on one scan · Run the public measured example.

docs.title: Follow one Wi-Fi scan through the pipeline
docs.text: This guided walkthrough explains what the repository does to one scan. The descriptions are conceptual; numeric examples are illustrative and should not be read as archived study findings.

docs.title: Step 1. Receive a query scan
docs.text:
A scan lists observed AP labels and signal strengths, for example:

{"AP1": -61, "AP4": -76, "AP7": -83}

The labels are stable within a data unit. In the released HK data, AP1 and AP4 are pseudonymous labels, not real MAC addresses. Received signal strength (RSS) is measured in dBm; less negative numbers generally indicate stronger received signals.

docs.title: Step 2. Compare it with a radio map
docs.text:
A radio map is a table of training Wi-Fi fingerprints paired with known local positions. It is not a photograph or architectural floor plan. The pipeline compares the query's RSS values and observed APs with the training fingerprints.

Radio-map role Contents Why needed Reference fingerprint Observed APs and RSS measurements Compare signal patterns Reference position Local X and Y (and categorical floor when available) Associate matches with a location Evaluation query Observed APs and held-out known position Generate prediction and evaluate it retrospectively

docs.title: Step 3. Retrieve candidate reference points
docs.text: The implementation retrieves the most relevant candidate fingerprints. For the publicly computed integrity outputs, each query is associated with ten diagnostic candidates. The candidate file contains their ranks and relative metric coordinates.

docs.title: Step 4. Positioning and integrity run alongside each other
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    A[Query + retrieved candidates] --> P[Estimator]
    A --> I[Diagnostic indicators]
    P --> X[Estimated position]
    I --> B[Scan-level features]
    B --> C[Five SQS components]
    C --> S[SQS, C_sigma, FII]
    X --> O[Location estimate with support evidence]
    S --> O

A positioning estimator, such as KNN or WKNN, uses reference fingerprints to infer a coordinate. The reliability layer evaluates the strength and spatial consistency of the evidence, not simply a second copy of the coordinate.

docs.title: Step 5. Summarize evidence using SQS
docs.text: SQS combines five normalized components with equal nominal weights. Component scaling is relative to a reference cohort; it must not be interpreted as a calibrated probability of correctness.

docs.title: Step 6. Inspect the output
docs.text:
Each test scan generates an entry in Uxx_scan_reliability.csv.gz. The matching Uxx_retrieved_candidates.csv.gz gives the supporting reference candidates. A reader can ask:

  • How many APs were observed?
  • Were the fingerprint matches similar?
  • Were the candidates spatially concentrated or dispersed?
  • How did these properties contribute to SQS?
  • Is any warning rule independently calibrated for the intended use?

For the four public empirical units, the code generates 5,041 scan-feature rows and 50,410 candidate rows.

What this walkthrough does not claim

Running the indicator layer on public input does not retrain the eight original ESWA estimators, independently calibrate an online warning system, or regenerate every historical manuscript value.

Explore an actual measured scan: Interactive scan-to-SQS explorer.

Next: Run the actual code · Read the generated outputs.

docs.title: Which results prove what?
docs.text:
A reproducible software example, a stored research result, and a freshly retrained model are not interchangeable. This project makes these evidence levels explicit so that anyone using the repository can understand what they can execute and what has been archived.

Evidence type Where What is verified What is not claimed Fresh public measured-data computation scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py, examples/empirical_integrity/ Scan-level feature and SQS calculation on four released measured units Original historical eight-estimator predictions or prospective alarm validation New HK estimator baseline scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode hk-u09 Existing KNN/WKNN/Random Forest training and held-out 2D scoring The full manuscript experiment Original HK stored results results/empirical/hk_u09/ 831 scans, eight stored estimator outputs and recorded decisions; consistency checks Re-fitting all original models and achieving byte-for-byte equality Approved research summaries results/approved/ Archived aggregate analysis over ten units/eight estimators, checked for integrity Reconstructing missing measurements or proprietary source recordings Fully synthetic test fixture examples/synthetic_combined/ and dashboard/ Pipeline integration and software examples Experimental evidence about actual positioning accuracy

docs.title: Research evaluation scope
docs.text:
The original experiment used 10 units, 54,520 training scans, 13,629 test scans and eight estimators. Its analyses concerned associations between diagnostic quantities and positioning error, gross-error diagnosis, floor-aware behavior, SQS ablation, and computation time.

The four measured units distributed here are U01–U03 and U09. For U04–U08 and U10, obtain the source data from publishers. A newly formatted or newly split copy may be useful for a scientific extension, but is not automatically identical to the harmonized original.

docs.title: Reproduce and inspect responsibly
docs.text:
python scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py
python scripts/check_public_integrity_release.py
python scripts/verify_existing_research_assets.py

The first command computes new outputs. The next two validate committed records and historical research assets. None of these commands, by itself, establishes a complete eight-estimator retraining of the ten-unit manuscript study.

The numerical checker permits a documented 0.001 difference in U09 mean/median SQS across supported numerical environments, with per-scan drift reported; near-tie candidate rankings can differ. It does not silently replace frozen historical values.

docs.title: Scientific and deployment cautions
docs.text:
• SQS is relative scan-support information, not a calibrated per-scan probability of correctness.
  • A low or high indicator is not a universal error rule across every building or device.
  • Historical Android post-retrieval diagnostic computation timing is not full scan-to-position latency.
  • Real floor-plan images/vectors and source HK AP identities are not published.

Further reading: Reproducibility boundaries · Original research asset guide · Calibration.

docs.title: How to read one scan-level result
docs.text: The main public empirical output contains one row per held-out Wi-Fi scan. It describes the observed signals, match support, candidate geometry and composite diagnostic scores. The accompanying candidate table lets you inspect the ten reference fingerprints retrieved for that query.

docs.title: Three files to know
docs.text:
Name Source How to interpret it Uxx_scan_reliability.csv.gz Fresh indicator computation One row per scan; individual indicators and SQS, C_sigma, FII Uxx_retrieved_candidates.csv.gz Diagnostic candidate retrieval Ten ranked candidate reference positions per scan summary.json Verification metadata Counts, mean/median SQS, and source-input checksums

The freshly calculated files are written to results/public_integrity/. Examples of the same output types are checked into examples/empirical_integrity/.

docs.title: Questions to ask for each scan
docs.text:
1. What did the device see? Start with AP count and RSS statistics. A query with fewer visible APs may have weaker fingerprint support, but no single indicator decides reliability on its own.

2. How well did the query match the radio map? Inspect RSS distance, cosine similarity, overlap and AP-set novelty. A strong signal match does not guarantee that candidate locations are spatially close.

3. Do retrieved reference points agree spatially? Inspect candidate spread (sigma_fps), candidate-set diameter (D_cand) and neighborhood instability (I_k). These tell different stories from RSS match alone.

4. Is there good local reference support? Examine the local reference-point density and nearest-reference distances.

5. What does the composite summarize? SQS uses five components: signal match, candidate geometry, AP count, overlap and density. It uses cohort-relative scaling and is not a probability of correct positioning.

See the full 18-indicator reference for exact output column names and adverse directions.

docs.title: Scan and candidate rows align by ID
docs.text:
The row_id field identifies the scan in the scan-level file and associates it with the candidate rows. For each scan, the public integrity example stores exactly 10 candidate ranks. Across four units, this yields 5,041 scan rows and 50,410 candidate rows.

Three different concepts

  • Positioning error (metres): requires a position prediction and a ground-truth reference.
  • SQS: reports normalized scan/radio-map support, not error in metres.
  • Gross-error warning: a rule that must define its threshold and reference/calibration cohort. It is not automatically produced as an independently validated future alarm by the public scan-feature command.

docs.text:
The four-unit public computation summary records:

Unit Test scans Diagnostic candidate rows U01 1,157 11,570 U02 1,101 11,010 U03 1,952 19,520 U09 831 8,310 Total 5,041 50,410

docs.title: Quick start: measured Wi-Fi input to indicator results
docs.text:
This route runs the existing research source code on four real-data units included in GitHub: U01–U03 from UJIIndoorLoc and the relative-coordinate HK U09 subset.

No access-point hardware required

You only need Python and the released data files to reproduce this offline evaluation. The Android app and a live phone scan are not required.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer, recommended 3.11 or 3.12.
  • Git and a command-line terminal.
  • The package dependencies in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: 1. Download the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AhmedMansoour/wifi-fingerprinting-scan-level-reliability.git
cd wifi-fingerprinting-scan-level-reliability

docs.title: 2. Install the research environment
docs.text:
python -m pip install -e ".[dev,empirical]"

The empirical option pins the numerical libraries used for the published held-out HK baseline checks.

docs.title: 3. Compute scan-level reliability from measured data
docs.text:
python scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py

This runs the original reliability code on 20,157 training and 5,041 query scans. It writes new files under the ignored results/public_integrity/ folder; it does not modify the archived study outputs.

docs.title: 4. Inspect and check the outputs
docs.text:
python scripts/check_public_integrity_release.py

The checker validates scan IDs, row counts, ten retrieved candidate ranks per query and exact SQS arithmetic in the stored public examples.

File What you will see results/public_integrity/U09_scan_reliability.csv.gz One scan's indicator values and composite outputs per row results/public_integrity/U09_retrieved_candidates.csv.gz Ten ranked candidate reference points per scan results/public_integrity/summary.json Rows processed, SQS summaries and source file hashes

docs.title: Shorter run: HK U09 only
docs.text:
python scripts/reproduce_public_integrity.py --units U09

To compare this fresh U09 run with the committed example, run:

python scripts/check_public_integrity_release.py --check-fresh

The comparison checks the same 831 scan identities and aggregate mean/median SQS within a documented 0.001 tolerance; it reports per-scan numerical differences due to candidate near-ties.

docs.title: Also try a positioning estimator
docs.text:
python scripts/reproduce_release.py --mode hk-u09

That separate baseline trains KNN, WKNN and Random Forest and evaluates them against held-out 2D positions. It is not the original full eight-estimator historical reproduction.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Problem First check Missing wifi_integrity package Run the editable installation from the repository root Missing .csv.gz inputs Confirm data/empirical/ and data/radio_maps/ were cloned Different run summaries Compare Python/dependency versions and numerical backend, then use the documented aggregate tolerance Looking for U04–U08 or U10 See the official download and conversion guide

Next: Understand the CSV outputs · See exact reproducibility boundaries.

docs.title: Run the workflow with your own Wi-Fi data
docs.text: To process an external dataset, you need authorized fingerprint measurements, a training radio map, and a held-out query set. The repository includes a CSV converter and the same harmonization functions used by the research code.

docs.title: Canonical eight-column CSV
docs.text:
dataset,group,split,row_id,floor,x,y,rss_json
Field Meaning dataset, group Unit identifiers consistent with config/datasets.yaml split train for the radio map, test for queries row_id Unique row identifier within the unit floor Categorical integer or -1 if unavailable x, y Local, finite coordinates in metres with a shared origin and scale rss_json Observed AP/RSS dictionary such as {"AP1":-60.0}

Omit access points that are not observed rather than inserting invented RSS readings. Do not include original BSSIDs, participant identifiers, SSIDs or site geometry unless you have a clear right and purpose to distribute them.

docs.title: Prepare a publisher dataset
docs.text:
1. Download the actual files from the dataset's publisher page.
  2. Determine its RSS columns, coordinate columns, floor categories and missing-signal sentinel.
  3. Assign stable pseudonymous AP labels within that unit.
  4. Keep train/test assignments. A new split is not the historical ESWA split.
  5. Write a gzip-compressed eight-column CSV (one unit per file).

Use scripts/import_external_unit.py to convert wide or paired RSS/coordinate tables. Example CLI options are provided in the detailed formatting guide.

docs.title: Build native radio-map matrices
docs.text:
For a prepared U04 file placed under LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS/U04.csv.gz:

python scripts/stage_existing_units.py \
  --input-dir LOCAL_MEASURED_UNITS --units U04 --allow-custom-splits

The script creates processed unit matrices and a training-only AP vocabulary. Once prepared, the existing code can run a supported native positioning baseline:

python -m wifi_integrity benchmark-native \
  --units U04 --estimators knn,wknn --output-name u04_native.csv.gz

Do not claim a paper reproduction after changing the split

Reformatting publisher input makes the code usable on those measurements. Reproducing the archived paper requires the same source version, split, AP mapping, preprocessing, estimator settings, and evaluation protocol.
